This study examines the connection between included particle production and fluid dynamic behavior in the collisions of lead ions at 2.76 TeV, specifically analyzing the elliptic flow (v2) in event shapes. By categorizing the particle yields from collisions of lead ions at 5.02 TeV and 2.56 TeV into two particles that exhibit an anisotropic distribution, researchers have discovered a strong correlation with an increasing trend of v2 as kinetic energy decreases. To understand this phenomenon, scientists employed several observables to describe the characteristics of the particle distribution, and it is shown that an effective scalar kinetic energy parameter can effectively capture the relationship between v2 and the particle spectrum. Furthermore, this study found that the value of this parameter is consistently around 440 MeV for all collisions regardless of the energy level, indicating that this parameter is intrinsically linked to the particle production and the development of the anisotropic particle distribution.

This paper introduces a novel class of anti-unitary operators, specifically tailored to the quaternion linear canonical Fourier transform (QLCFT). We have devised criteria to characterize functions and quaternions within this transformation framework, then established a distinct inequality as well as an associated inequality to determine functions with minimal energy dispersion under QLCFT. Furthermore, we introduce an infinitesimal variation principle that can yield both a characteristic equation and an optimal operator for a function identical to itself under QLCFT.

We've determined the maximum possible extremal GDoF benefit associated with an optimal power control method in a $K$ user symmetric interference network. Furthermore, we've established lower and upper limits for the extremal GDoF benefit offered by a linear power control method. Our research indicates that the extremal GDoF benefit offered by the optimal power control method grows at a rate of $\Theta(\sqrt{K})$ when $K$ is a large number, as do the limits for the extremal GDoF benefit offered by the binary and linear power control methods. Consequently, we've proven that the extremal GDoF benefit provided by the optimal power control method is $\Theta(\sqrt{K})$ when $K$ is a large number, as are the lower limits for the extremal GDoF benefit offered by the binary power control method when $K$ is a large number, as well as the $\Theta(\sqrt{K})$ limits for the extremal GDoF benefit offered by the linear power control method.

A novel approach has been devised for multiple-time-step schemes in particle simulation, which involves vying for the most accurate and feasible small time steps for different processes by utilizing their respective scales.v  传统的多时间步长方案存在不对称的结构,这使得时间步长的优化变得困难,尤其是当需要同时模拟多个过程时. 为了解决这个问题,我们引入了一种新的双对数时间步长确定公式,通过平衡主要过程的模拟精度和次要过程的数值稳定性来实现小时间步长的最佳选择.  这种方法可以应用于多种粒子模拟场景,包括多个不同尺度粒子的模拟.  对于每个粒子,我们分别确定适合其自自由路径回归的时间步长,从而确保所有粒子在指定时间步长内的行为合理.  为了处理次要过程,我们根据次要过程的数值稳定性需求来调整次要变量的时间步长,从而确保所有次要过程在模拟中保持稳定.

This article will examine the equation $a^2+ab+b^2=7^n$ in detail, offering proven insights for multiple whole number conditions on $n$. We will establish an infinite number of instances where whole number solutions $a, b, b'$ exist for given odd whole number values of $n$, specifically when $7^{(n-1)/2}$ is factored into prime components, there will be at least three sets of whole number pairs that satisfy the condition, thereby demonstrating at least three solutions for the original equation.

This paper presents an innovative approach to modeling a single-legged hopping robot operating on a viscoelastic surface. It outlines the dynamics of a one-degree-of-freedom hopper and develops a simplified surface model. Using this model, the surface forces and the hopping leg's movement are calculated, and a viscoelastic parameter is proposed to adjust the simulated environment. The simulation demonstrates how the proposed model affects the hopping leg's movement and energy, and the results show the surface's impact on the leg's movement and energy as the viscoelastic parameter changes.

A flexible parametric model is based on a series expansion in a dimensionless variable, effectively bridging perturbative and non-perturbative QCD regimes. This series enables the exchange of only a few parameters while maintaining accuracy and physical constraints, such as the BL sum rule, for both proton and meson (pion, kaon) two-body systems. This series is based on a flexible parametric model which is capable of estimating LC QCD moments and applying a dispersion relation to derive LC QCD octet and moment BMLs. The model predicts meson FPs, masses, decay constants, and KL transition, as well as pionic QCD sum rules.

A previously observed phenomenon, droplet electrohydrodynamic instability, in liquid masses is now shown to occur in a droplet as small as 0.5 millimeters in diameter. In this study, we have characterized the motion of polystyrene acetobutylolate coated with stearic acid methyl ester in a mixture of suspended dry ice aerosols. Without considering evaporation, which is slowed down by the surrounding ice particles, numerical simulations indicate that the movement of a coated droplet aligns well with observed breakup patterns, particularly at higher concentrations of aerosols.

Effective communication skills, including a sophisticated understanding of negation, are a hallmark of famously fictional characters like Sherlock Holmes.
However, humans possess even more advanced thinking abilities, including a heightened ability to process negation, and we want our artificial intelligence systems to mimic this.
To test and train models on this very ability, we need a challenging dataset that poses a genuine (not deceptively easy) understanding of negation.
To this end, we introduce CONDAQA, a highly demanding dataset for testing models' genuine ability to process negation, consisting of 12,000 complex entities and relationships that are either denied or constrained, extracted from the TAC-R dataset after filtering out straightforward examples.
As anticipated, current models struggle with tasks involving negated or constrained information, showing a significant drop in performance compared to baseline information, indicating a deficiency in understanding these more subtle pieces of information.
Notably, we find that large language models also exhibit a significant difficulty with the CONDAQA dataset, leading us to explore a range of model-training approaches to enhance their performance, ultimately resulting in a system that significantly surpasses baseline performance.

The concept of hierarchy has been extensively studied in the fields of psychology and neuroscience, and recent empirical data supports the widely accepted theory that human and animal navigation abilities are rooted in cognitive structures organized hierarchically. Over the last decade, researchers have begun applying hierarchical metrics to map and analyze complex systems, including navigational networks, and have discovered that these systems exhibit pronounced modular and fractal characteristics. Despite these significant breakthroughs, the assessment of hierarchical cognitive structures and complex networks remains a cognitively demanding and time-consuming process, which has led to the development of automated algorithms for computing hierarchical indices, such as minimum free energy, hierarchical modularity, and multi-scale modularity. In an effort to facilitate the analysis of large-scale networks, we have reviewed and compared four scalable framework options for computing hierarchical modularity, and we have introduced and made available an original framework that is capable of processing networks comprising up to tens of millions of nodes within minutes to hours.

A crucial aspect of understanding quantum annealing (QA) lies in identifying the time scale at which the system transitions from its initial state to a entangled many-body ground state, often associated with a quench dynamics period. Previous studies generally assumed this transition occurs abruptly, typically around the point where the transverse field is comparable to the coupling strength, a so-called interaction-driven transition. Conversely, our research reveals that for disordered QA models such as the random exact cover problem, there exists an distinct period during which the system behaves like a mean-field theory, and is actually when it is most beneficial to execute QA. In this specific interval, the system's ground state exhibits a mean field behavior, and is where a clear distinction in the evolution of the system's effective annealing time exponent can be clearly observed. Furthermore, we observe that this meaningful scale is directly related to the system's lowest excitation energy, and that a significant portion of literature discussing the potential of QA has thus far remained elusive due to the lack of clear identification of this specific dynamics.

In the analysis of complex systems, testing methods have been successfully employed, however, they can only confirm correct behavior for specific input sequences. Therefore, they are limited in ensuring the system's correct operation across all possible user interactions. To overcome this challenge, model checking and runtime verification techniques have been developed, although, they are incapable of handling situations where traces contain errors or ambiguities. This work proposes an extension to partial functions in prefix and suffix code, then examines the consequences of this change and explores the feasibility of using this framework for conformance verification in situations with defined, discontinuous traces.

Researchers have noticed that a single Fermi surface seems to be sufficient to explain the superconducting properties of infinite-layer nickelate, even though its theoretical model suggests a multi-band system. To investigate this phenomenon, we computed the single-band character of each band by comparing the diagonal and non-diagonal components of its density matrix. The results showed that the lower band has a significantly higher single-band character, primarily located at the nickel site, which is responsible for superconductivity. Conversely, the upper band's density matrix exhibits large off-diagonal elements indicative of strong screening effects, thereby limiting its contribution to superconductivity. The screening effects at the level of the density matrix provide a straightforward mechanism to account for the superconducting behavior of the infinite-layer nickelate system.

This paper examines the phase dynamics of the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation under specific initial conditions in three-dimensional space. We demonstrate that for a sufficiently small collision cross-section, the interaction between shear flow and collisional diffusion causes distinct gas phases to blend into a equilibrium state, where maximal dispersion causes phases with opposite collisions to combine into a maximal sum. Moreover, we derive a precise rate at which the resulting phase decays over time.

We re-examine the analysis of sea surface imagery conducted by Cox and Munk in 1954, a study for which they employed natural sunlight and a 25 cm telescope to obtain images. Using a 3.9 mm channel of satellite radiometer IASI, a more powerful instrument with a 0.5cm aperture, we obtained sea surface observations of the Mediterranean Sea on October 12, 2019, under similar lighting conditions. We find that wave slopes follow a Gaussian distribution and that wind speeds derived from both sets of observations are in good agreement, with our new data showing lower wave slopes corresponding to lower wind speeds.

When designing large-scale test cases for a software system, the objective is to minimize the combined number of test failure indicators when at least one test case in each functional module reports a failure. This study addresses this issue by formulating it as a test case selection problem and modeling matrix rows as test cases, then applies singular value decomposition to a test failure indicator matrix to identify an optimal solution. A test case choice algorithm is developed, and its efficiency is enhanced through parallelization, and the algorithm's steps are explained, and the algorithm's efficiency is demonstrated through experimental results, and the test's purpose and results are shown, and the algorithm's efficiency is demonstrated, and it is shown that the parallelized algorithm significantly improves the test's efficiency.

The COVID-19 pandemic significantly altered daily life, prompting a detailed analysis of its impact on social behavior, including sentiment expression on various platforms. This study focuses on classifying tweets related to COVID-19 and their underlying sentiment by utilizing and optimizing several sentiment analysis techniques, ultimately achieving a 79.11% accuracy rate with a combined Bi-Graded LSTMs model.

A theoretical framework is proposed based on the interlayer tunneling concept, adapted for the 1990s understanding of cuprate superconductors, which differs significantly from the 1980s structure understood at the time Anderson's original theory was conceived. Key features of cuprates, such as their planar CuO2 structure and various periodic electronic patterns not present in high-temperature cuprate compounds, necessitate important distinctions from the original interlayer tunneling models. A revised version of this theory is then presented, incorporating these revised concepts.

Research into the interior of neutron stars has revealed the sound speed within the dense matter there may approach or even surpass the relativistic limit, indicating the existence of strange quark matter. If this is accurate, it could significantly impact our understanding of the composition of neutron stars. By utilizing the MIT bag model, we've been able to calculate the sound speed as a function of density, revealing a distinctive inflection point. If the bag parameter is set to its physically meaningful value, the sound speed would inevitably exceed the speed of light in densities relevant to neutron stars, as evidenced by their maximum mass capabilities.

For any disordered labeled tree of length n, we examine the minimum distance
between any pair of edges. A Tauberian analysis is provided to understanding the
properties of this minimum distance when n increases without bound. This understanding
enables us to prove that the expected value of this distance among trees of length n
can be scaled to an integer, and for large values of n, the probability of this occurring
approaches one. Furthermore, this result allows us to prove that a random disordered
tail-closed polygon of length 2n can be constructed from a random disordered tail-closed
polygon of length n by forming pairs of symbols and connecting them if their second
indices match, using the expected value as the disordered taic index of this graph.

A new type of entangled state, the "compass state," is being extensively studied due to its high applicability in modeling quantum compression and displacement effects. This research demonstrates that, unlike their classical counterparts, compressing or displacing the compass state only moderately reduces its entanglement, which remains robust against these disturbances. This indicates that the quantum compass state possesses the necessary stability for practical uses in quantum communication systems. Furthermore, the effect of noise on the compass state reveals that, under certain conditions, it behaves similarly to a Gaussian state, which enables more efficient detection of quantum phases during demonstrations.

A theoretical model is developed to understand the vertical shear instability at the edge of a protoplanetary disk, taking into account the grain growth and sedimentation of dust. The model reveals that the critical temperature gradient required to sustain the instability increases with grain size. By around 10 Angstroms, the critical gradient returns to the value predicted for a system with continuous dust. The model predicts the onset of sedimentation of gas-supported solid bodies in the millimeter wavelength range. However, the mean free path of hydrogen molecules may become comparable to the disk height, allowing the disk to cool below its adiabatic threshold, thus sustaining the shear instability.

This research focuses on harmonic functions within the context of a particular type of manifold where the Ricci curvature decreases over time. We have established a key theorem which asserts that any continuous function on this manifold with an upper bound on its Laplacian that remains constant throughout must be a constant itself. This holds particularly true when the manifold exhibits a uniform scalar curvature. As a result, we were able to demonstrate that any bounded harmonic function on a parabolic model space that remains constant throughout is necessarily a constant, providing a alternative to previous proofs.

Recent advancements in deep learning have achieved significant breakthrough across various industries, but one pressing concern related to neural network defenses is that related work primarily focuses on static backdoors. In contrast, dynamically operable backdoors are more challenging to detect due to their apparent normal operation. A statically detectable backdoor can be considered dynamic, but utilizing the mechanism of shared weights in the last layer of the network, which computes the global mean pooling, allows for the creation of a truly functional dynamic backdoor. This novel approach enables the creation of a backdoor trigger that operates effectively with the same hidden unit, and can be easily adapted to other models employing the global mean pooling mechanism.

The influence of post-Newtonian gravity on modern-day and Gaia-like astrometry is being re-evaluated, with a focus on how the PPN parameter gamma affects the measurement of parallaxes, proper motions, and the overall $\delta \chi^2$ in the Gaia data. As the accuracy of satellite astrometry improves, the data will in the future be more sensitive to relativistic effects, potentially allowing for the determination of key parameters like the PPN parameter gamma from the data itself. Moreover, the variability of solar gravitational influences on parallax variability and the proposed approach of incorporating a rank-2 tensor term in the Baïcon code to avoid the bias of proper motion estimates caused by the unaccounted parallax variability are also examined. The study finds that the unaddressed post-Newtonian effects result in a $\delta \chi^2$ of around 0.15 for the Gaia data, a negligible impact of curvature and semi-major axis variations of the light cones of the solar gravitational influence on the parallax variability, and the impact of the unmodeled variation on the global $\delta \chi^2$, the precision of parallax $\sigma_\varpi$, and proper motion $\sigma_\mu$ estimates for the Gaia $\beta$ and $\delta \chi^2$ metrics.

Model reduction is much desired for complex models as it makes them easier to analyze and control, and also accelerates their simulation, which is crucial in fields like astronomy where observations are frequent and in systems biology, where experiments are time-consuming and costly. Generally, model reduction techniques are divided into two categories: physical methods, which rely on the structure of the original model, and data-driven methods. However, physical methods are limited to specific types of models and dynamical systems, often requiring the original model to be in a specific form, like state-space, which is not always feasible for complex systems. Moreover, in systems biology and astronomy, where modeling is experimental, modelers do not have full access to the underlying dynamics of the system and must make numerous assumptions to develop their models. This study presents a technique to convert complex, high-dimensional models into simpler ones that preserve their underlying dynamics, even when they are not in state-space form, by using an iterative and robust method that makes minimal assumptions about the model's complexity. This technique is experimentally evaluated on complex models of atmospheric dynamics, biological models, and is publicly available on a public repository.

A well-known feature of lower-dimensional systems is spontaneous current generation, which can be observed in the form of magnetization in polymers or spin waves in films, typically requiring an external power. Contrary to this, we have discovered a self-sustained current in a one-component Bose-Einstein condensate that does not break up and creates self-localized dark-bright structures. These structures, which consist of two interacting parts, generate opposite currents in each component and become self-trapped as a result of the mean-field effect. Notably, these structures can support multiple modes of oscillation, where they exchange energy with an external pump and recover their initial state, demonstrating robustness. This work paves the way for stable multi-mode states with self-generated interactions in BEC systems.

This project addresses the challenge of protecting machine learning (ML) model predictions from being manipulated by untrusted users who have already obtained the model. Building upon a previously developed system called SIMC, which employed a binary search technique to protect against malicious users, our new version, SIMC 2.0, features two key enhancements: Firstly, we introduce an optimized technique to more accurately pinpoint the attempt at prediction manipulation, thereby reducing communication costs by a factor of two; Secondly, we expand the protection scope to include a variety of attack methods, such as those targeting specific layers, and can even handle scenarios where the malicious users have access to both training and inference data, although this comes with increased security risks.

Our analysis of fast antenna for studies of tons of molecular and atomic targets in the M101 galaxy group and surroundings, revealed two distinct types of anomalies. First, we found six nebulous structures, resembling nebulae, with no visible galaxies within 50 kiloparsecs, which could be nebulous galaxies without a visible core, or nebulae sustained by gravity of nearby stars. These findings may be related to dark matter halos, or both. Notably, one of these nebulae, located near the galaxy M101, could be sustained by dark matter alone, which may offer important insights for cosmologists. Additionally, a large halo of dark matter could be found around the galaxy M101. Furthermore, a prominent atomica hydrogen tail was detected, which is not frequently observed, and could be related to atomica hydrogen evaporation, or atomica hydrogen being pushed away by stellar winds and radiation from nearby galaxies. These discoveries will be discussed in light of atomica hydrogen dynamics and the effects of galaxy interactions.

To effectively tackle the challenge of answering questions that require a broad range of everyday knowledge, it is crucial to simultaneously consider both global meaning and detailed information. To achieve this, a novel approach is proposed that utilizes a combination of a BERT-based question builder and a BERT-based BFM network to effectively integrate semantic-related information while preventing over-reliance on prior knowledge. A unique dataset, Commonsense-QA, is created to evaluate this approach, which consists of a BERT-based question formulation that is supported by a rich amount of entity, edge, node and document-related information. Experimental results, which include both controlled and real-world scenarios, demonstrate the effectiveness of this proposed method.

Astronomical sources such as the upper atmospheres of planets, comets, and small solar system bodies are home to a rich array of molecular cations based on hydrogen frameworks, including OH+, N2H+, and CO+. These species are crucial for understanding the composition and chemical processes occurring in these environments, especially OH+ which is essential for tracking water in the cometary environment. Despite their significance, many of these molecular cations are not well understood, with only the spectra of some available in the wavelength range of near-infrared to ultraviolet light. As a result, their abundance and chemical behavior remain difficult to assess in these environments. As part of preparing the road towards OH+ detection in the cometary environment, a detailed examination of the spectral gaps in O2, NO, and N2 molecular cations was conducted using the open community astrophysical database, KASTA+. This examination identified specific spectral regions that are most desirable for future experiments, with the cations' spectra being influenced by the underlying neutral atom interactions as a result of exchange correlations in the system.

Given a global field F of characteristic not equal to 2, and n variables, we examine positive-definite rectangles defined by inequalities involving products of coordinates. Assuming these rectangles are contained within the field^n, we establish that their combined area is bounded by a constant times f^(n-1), where the constant depends on the properties of the field and f represents the minimum distance between any two distinct points formed by varying the coordinates.

The burgeoning field of exoplanet exploration demands a significant advancement in detection sensitivity and precision, a goal that can be realized through the application of photonic technology. This approach, known as astrophotony, has already made a notable impact on radial velocity exploration and is now being pushed to its limits to tackle a wider range of planetary detections and astrophysical analyses via spectral cross-correlation techniques. These methods, which involve comparing a observed spectrum with a high-fidelity spectral template, are sensitive to even the minuscule distortions and signals that cannot be detected by more conventional radial velocity methods. As such, they are exceedingly precise, but as a consequence, they are also exceptionally vulnerable to sources of noise and cross-talk that can result in detection biases and inaccuracies in data interpretation. This paper delves into a wider array of spectral cross-correlation techniques and their underlying photonic principles to pinpoint the sources of distortion and signal at a granular level, thereby facilitating more accurate interpretations of data and more sensitive detections and analyses via these methods.

In the last few years, multiple modeling approaches using deep learning in the realm of drug relationship prediction have emerged, but a singular comprehensive framework that encapsulates them all has not yet been achieved. In this study, a flexible and all-encompassing deep learning model is presented, which can be viewed as a unified perspective on previous models. It incorporates several popular relational representation techniques, including the use of hash-based, set-based and ordered relations, in a singular model. A new, previously undeveloped relational pattern is also included in this framework. Through comprehensive experiments and in-depth analysis, it is demonstrated that this model achieves the best performance to date on three widely used benchmarks in this field. Furthermore, the analysis provided in this paper offers insights into the significance of different relational patterns and has the potential to guide the selection of suitable models for various applications.

The primary objective of this paper is to establish an Itô-Wentzell formula that accounts for boundary effects resulting from the interaction of rough paths with a well-defined boundary, or manifold, within $\mathbb{R}^d$. To achieve this, we consider the semimartingale type weak solutions of the parabolic equation, utilizing the theory of rough paths and then extending our findings to include rough coefficients and a broader class of rough paths than previously used in existing literature.

In the context of machine learning, it is a well-known fact that a model is poised to overfit when the training data is skewed. This issue is particularly prevalent in the realm of Federated Learning when the training data is significantly heterogeneous. To tackle this problem, we introduced an innovative approach known as Stroll for Learning (S4L), which involves a stochastic adjustment of the local data transformations at regular intervals. This method allows for a stochastic exploration of the space of transformations, thereby providing greater flexibility to learn from heterogeneous data without inspecting it. The S4L approach also facilitates the learning process by prioritizing the adaptation to regions of the space where the dataset is concentrated, all while maintaining a low communication overhead with the server. The effectiveness of S4L was validated through experiments on the Iris dataset and MobileNet architecture, leading to substantial accuracy improvements in settings involving heterogeneous data.

Three-dimensional wave turbulence is a complex, vector phenomenon that combines the dynamics of irrotational waves and energy cascades. We employed numerical simulations to understand three-dimensional wave turbulence in a gL4B configuration, utilizing a high-accuracy spectral method that efficiently models a large number of interacting three-dimensional waves. Our simulations revealed a distinct, random pattern of energy distribution across frequencies that, when plotted on a logarithmic scale, resembles the predicted Zakharov-Kolmogorov spectrum. This discovery provides the first concrete evidence of wave turbulence's theoretical spectrum in three-dimensional space.

Individuals who interact with the criminal justice system often suffer from mental health issues that impede their ability to differentiate right from wrong. As a result, they may be tried as competent defendants, yet a significant portion continues to grapple with cognitive deficits. For those convicted of third-degree felonies and ordered to undergo psychological treatment, our analysis reveals an increased likelihood of returning to the justice system. This positive effect is more pronounced when the court specifies compliance as a condition of the psychological treatment order. Ultimately, psychological therapy seems to empower incarcerated individuals to regain their autonomy and make informed decisions.

A pervasive challenge in medical image segmentation is the scarcity of suitable training data. To overcome this limitation, semi-supervised learning has been extensively utilized, although it demands a substantial number of data pairs. We propose a novel approach that utilizes a single training image to optimize consistency regularization, a technique that has become a norm in medical image segmentation. We establish a strong link between our approach and the theoretical underpinnings ofPiA, a method that seeks to minimize regret in online learning. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach by adapting the Swin-UNet architecture and adapting consistency regularization to medical image segmentation through loss function suppression.

The ATLAS Jet Trigger System at the LHC needs a significant upgrade to handle increased luminosity and data processing demands. To adapt to the CMS Ultra scale architecture, a new processor-based board called HV2 has been created, utilizing advanced 5GPCIe FPGAs from Xilinx. This high-performance FPGA board features multiple components, including 24 10G SFP+ optical ports and a custom-designed deserializer to connect to the front-end detector system. Due to its powerful processing capabilities and flexibility, the FPGA system on board HV2 can run a range of detection and filtering algorithms to identify jets in real-time during LHC collisions. A prototype FPGA control system called ATLAS Jet Tracker (ATLJTrk) has been created to track and identify jets for the ATLAS detector, and testing of the HV2 board with this prototype revealed excellent detection and timing performance.

In the field of Computer Graphics and Virtual Reality, creating lifelike 3D human avatars that can express a wide range of emotions and movements is a significant challenge.  A crucial aspect of this challenge involves accurately representing joint rotations, as errors in this area can cause noticeable discrepancies in avatar movement and facial expressions. To address this issue, we present ANR, a framework based on conditional normalizing flows that allows for the realistic visualization of articulated 3D human bodies. ANR can reconstruct complex poses from single images and expresses emotions through blended shape and motion components conditioned on retargeting masks. Evaluations using public datasets demonstrate that ANR outperforms existing methods in terms of pose accuracy and overall quality.

A critical aspect of designing stable systems in chaotic environments is understanding and predicting the influence of initial conditions on long-term dynamics. This study reveals that a singular metric can effectively measure the impact of perturbation on the dynamics of an isolated atom by analyzing the difference in a relevant quantity between the atom's and an unstuck state as a function of time. Our findings are supported by an innovative approach that employs a graph neural network to predict the atom's dynamics from an experimental data of its ionization frequency, and validates this approach with experiments on a hydrogen atom trapped in a radio-frequency trap.

Consider a scenario where we have $p$ distinct distributions, denoted as $\mathcal{P} = \{\mathcal{P}_1, \dots, \mathcal{P}_p\}$, and for any combination of these distributions, we have a mixture distribution, defined as $\sum_{i=1}^p \theta_i \mathcal{P}_i$, where the weights $\theta_i$ sum to one. Suppose we are given $n$ independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) observations from this mixture distribution. The paper proves that, in situations where the dimensions of the parameters of the distributions in $\mathcal{P}$ are finite, and assuming the distributions are identifiable, it is possible to show that the maximum likelihood estimator of the mixture distribution converges at a rate of $\sqrt{n}$ to its true value. Specifically, it is proven that, for any set of distributions in $\mathcal{P}$, either all dimensions are less than or equal to two, and the estimated maximum likelihood converges at a rate of $\sqrt{n}$, or if any estimated dimension is greater than two, it is proven that the estimated higher-dimension parameters do not converge at a rate of $\sqrt{n}$, and thus cannot be used to estimate the average of the parameters. This limitation is demonstrated with an application to a two-part sampling method, and the proposed solution of estimating the average of parameters is shown to be efficient.

Integrating Automatic Knowledge Tracing (KT) models with Adaptive Learning (AL) systems has been demonstrated to outperform traditional non-deep learning based KT and testing techniques. Outperforming non-deep learning based KT models, deep learning models achieve superior performance through more precise student knowledge state estimations. However, evaluating these models requires access to ground truth data, which is inaccessible in real-world scenarios. This paper presents pyKT, an open-source Python library that facilitates the evaluation of multiple deep learning based KT models and streamlines their integration with AL algorithms. By providing a unified interface, pyKT enables researchers to seamlessly compare the performance of different deep learning based KT and testing models in simulated real-world knowledge tracing scenarios. Furthermore, the library will be released to the public, and its documentation and setup instructions are available at this link: http://pykt.org/.

Given a variety $X$ and an elliptic operator P defined on it, we demonstrate that the range of P is closed in $C^\infty(X)$ if and only if the kernel of P is finite-dimensional. This result implies that D-bundles over algebraic varieties of dimension at least 1 do not contain degenerate bundles.

This paper discusses the development of the Alethe format, a standardized set of rules that defines acceptable reasoning formats for various symbols in computer programs. The Alethe format has been adopted by multiple programs, including Kepler, CVC3, CVC4, E-prover, Paradox, and SMT-RU, which have the option to generate arguments in this format. Furthermore, the implementation of the Alethe format format is facilitated by the Alethe tools, specifically the Alethe TPT driver and the Alethe kernel, which can both validate and verify a wide range of programs' theorems.

Using unrestricted model changes in federated learning has significant benefits, but also poses security risks that must be managed. This work explores the challenges and opportunities presented by this approach, but the main contribution is a confirmation that UNR in a buffered asynchronous aggregation setting can prevent malicious attacks and is also analyzed mathematically. A new implementation of a secure buffered asynchronous framework is introduced, which excludes unrestricted models from malicious sources. The results show that excluding UNR from a malicious source does not negatively impact the model's accuracy. Furthermore, including UNR from a legitimate source improves convergence speed and final accuracy. These findings are demonstrated in a_f_ = 7F simulation with 50 iterations on the MNIST dataset.

Recently, end-to-end neural automatic speech recognition systems have achieved high accuracy on various tasks. Although these models excel at human speech processing, they fall short of biological processing efficiency due to the latter's ability to adapt and transfer learning abilities with imperfect audio. This study focuses on transferring knowledge and adapting models across languages, specifically examining whether a model trained on clear, high-quality speech can be effectively applied to its natural, noisy counterpart, or whether a model trained on noisy speech can be adapted to clear, high-quality speech. We investigate these concepts using three distinct datasets and present a simple, effective cross-language transfer approach. Our results demonstrate significant improvements in both scenarios, yielding models that outperform baseline systems in clear-to-noisy transfer and underperform not needed in the reverse.

The Twitch Users Profile (TUP) represents a real-world social network, composed of 2.3 million profiles of professional gamers who compete in various esports titles. TUP profiles include near neighbors (NN) of each user, which are other players frequently interacting with them in the network. The evaluation of node embedding techniques in network recommendation systems has been limited due to the lack of comprehensive datasets that provide NN information for all nodes. To address this limitation, we collected and released the Twitch Users Profile (TUP) dataset, containing 2.3 million profiles of professional gamers who compete in various esports titles. This dataset serves as a benchmark for evaluating node embedding techniques based on proximity and structural role preservation. In an experimental evaluation, we assessed different embedding methods, including embedding models focused on preserving the network's proximity and structural roles, using the TUP dataset. Our findings demonstrate that models which consider both aspects outperformed previous methods, with XAINO and TVAE emerging as the top-performing algorithms.

Our analysis suggests that any signals observed near 1500 MeV in the $M_K^0$ spectrum for $B^0\to \bar{K}^0\bar{K}^0$ are more likely attributed to $f_2(1420)$,而非 $f_X(1500)$. 基于这一结论的进一步研究, 我们将前因子中的 $f_X(1450)$ 替换为 $f_2(1420)$ 后, 理论预测与现有实验数据吻合度较高.

We propose a new concept called the Dark Dimension, suggesting a primordially small extra dimension made of Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) that constitute a significant fraction of the universe's dark matter. According to this idea, the 4D cosmological constant is merely a slice of an 11-dimensional Swampland formula for the M-theory vacuum, enabling an extremely dark energy value. The "Dark Substance" of the universe is comprised of Primordial Black Holes, which play a crucial role in forming a significant portion of the universe's matter. This study derives the density of PBHs based on the Swampland formula, which considers the dark energy vacuum. It is proposed that these Primordial Black Holes formed early in the universe's history, specifically when it was about $10^{-11}$ seconds old. Their mass is predicted to be within the range of $10^{6}-10^{7}$ kilograms, which means they emit Hawking radiation and contribute to the formation of dark matter through the production of dark radiation and other particles. This theory also proposes that PBHs constitute the "Dark Quark Stars" and the "Dark Neutron Stars" by creating heavy quarks and neutron through PBH collisions with neutron stars, which may be detected through their unique X-ray emission patterns.

A novel algorithm is proposed for the accurate force control of series elastic actuators (SEAs). The control method combines a robust transmission force observer with simple low-pass filtered force measurements, reducing the need for a highly compliant SEA shaft. By leveraging the intrinsic properties of SEAs, the proposed transmission force observer can significantly improve the tracking performance of the force control system. Theoretical analysis proves the asymptotic convergence of the estimation error and the advantage of using an SESA over a traditional SEA in terms of control bandwidth. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through theoretical simulation and comparison with existing methods.

A self-driven monolayer consisting of disc-shaped particles that can form kelp-rafts was analyzed. These clusters, rather than being continuous, exhibit gaps within them. It was discovered that as the density increases, both the size of the clusters and the proportion of particles within them that are connected will form non-linear increases. Surprisingly, a simple equation successfully predicted both rafts' integrity by accurately identifying the balance between edges and vertices of individual rafts. This formed the basis for defining a new parameter called the 'raft quality factor'. Furthermore, distinct rafts were identified in real-space and observed to be most prominent in a specific region of the medium density scope. A key insight was discovered when examining cluster-size distribution, which showed that it could be best described by a Cayley tree model, excluding any cluster interactions or structures that could be formed within the rafts.

A lattice gauge theory has been constructed in 3D for SU(Nc) with multiple scalar fields that can be oriented in the color direction, allowing for a lattice SU(Nc)/U(1)^{(Nc-1)^2} study when certain conditions are met. Using a group-theoretical method, the lattice action was reformulated, verifying its correctness for both SU(2) and SU(3) with Nf≥3, and Nf=2 for SU(3). The lattice SU(2) model was simulated for various coupling constants, and the results indicated that strong scalar interactions lead to a confining phase, while a new phase appears between the confined and deconfined phases. The deconfined phase is split into two subphases, a Higgs phase and a CMB phase, separated by a first-order transition. The origin of the new phase is explained by the direct interaction of scalar fields, and it exists for all SU(Nc) theories with Nc≥2 and Nf≥2. The nature of the boundary between the deconfined and new phases is unknown, but increasing Nc tends to expand the new phase, and the deconfined Higgs phase may be Higgsed for all Nc in a range of coupling constants. Achieving efficient and safe operation of underwater robots requires advanced control systems that can adapt to varying conditions and minimize energy use. This research combines machine learning and Gaussian processes to create an innovative control method, allowing for more effective robot performance. By training a difference learning model on a limited data set and using the model to predict the robot's performance, we developed a versatile controller that outperformed traditional techniques in terms of energy consumption and speed. When integrated with sparse kernels, the controller can generalize its learning and adapt to different robot scenarios, making it a more reliable and efficient solution for underwater robot performance optimization.

This paper proposes linear-time sorting networks with increased wire crossings per element, which can sort any partially ordered set of $n$ items. The innovation lies in reducing constant-depth network circuits, which has been a challenge in previous research. Although this trade-off results in slower element crossings, it still facilitates the development of versatile network applications in various fields such as hardware design, computer science, mathematics, and theory.

We employ a 1+1+2 covariant semi-tetrad method to describe a static, spherically symmetric relativistic star containing two interacting fluid layers with anisotropic pressures in the outer region and isotropic pressures in the inner region, and we derive the field equations in a covariant format, and obtain non-interacting fluid solutions by applying separation conditions for the interaction term, and apply these conditions to specific cases, and we provide the energy conditions and a proof of global regularity for the model's collapse, and we generate a density profile and a mass profile, and we illustrate the results with mass-radius data, and we illustrate the model's applicability to stellar collapse, and we conclude on the model's implications.

Using observational data from over a dozen galaxies similar to the Milky Way, 
we examined the relationship between the disk and outer structures of galaxy 
residents, specifically in relation to their age and metallicity. 
Our previous research suggested that these spiral patterns exist in multiple 
galaxies including the Milky Way. Furthermore, we discovered a consistent 
relationship between spiral parameters in various galaxies when scaled to 
material length scales. Building on our prior study, we developed a simplified 
equation of state for N-body simulations of two-component galaxies with up to 
10^12 solar masses of dark matter. Our current research focuses on describing 
and analyzing the results of these simulations to establish a method for 
modeling the formation and evolution of spiral structures in dark matter halos 
through a process known as "halo halo condensation."

Galactic mergers significantly influence galaxy evolution, with magnetic fields playing a crucial role in the formation of galaxies. During major mergers, extensive good-resolution simulations were conducted to examine the impact of moderate magnetic fields on galaxy formation processes. These simulations considered gravitational interactions, gas dynamics, magnetic field dynamics, as well as key processes such as radiative transfer, supermassive collisions, and mass ejections. The focus of the study was to investigate how magnetic fields affect galaxy features, especially during the merging process of two similarly massive galaxies. Based on the simulation, it was observed that although magnetic fields impede star formation due to their resistance, they also contribute to the creation of long-lived structures, including collapsed discs that maintain stability for over a billion years. Notably, this impact is observed in both merged and non-merged systems, where massive stellar discs and gas tails are formed and shaped by magnetic fields, resulting in long-lasting structures such as U-shaped stellar discs and extensive stellar trails.

The identification of severe COVID-19 cases through chest X-ray analysis is crucial for public health but is hindered by a lack of labeled data, especially for severe cases. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach called IAMCNet, which integrates two parts: a base network and a contrastive loss function to manage the imbalance of data. Experimentation on the Lidc19 dataset revealed that IAMCNet outperformed existing methods in accurately distinguishing severe COVID-19 cases from other disease variations or healthy scans.

This study examines multiple graph error correction tasks using both domain
adaptation and meta-learning approaches, specifically focusing on domain transfer
with limited training data for new languages or domains. We assess various few-shot
learning techniques on graph error correction and evaluate their performance across
different tasks and dataset configurations. To enhance domain transfer for graph
error correction, we propose a novel multi-task convolutional neural network with
shared and task-specific layers, along with an adaptive average ranking loss to
prioritize novel errors. We demonstrate that this approach successfully achieves
successful domain transfer even with small training datasets for new languages or
domains. We publicly release our code and models to facilitate future research in
this area.

When inferring discrete quantities from rounded averages, uncertainty plays a critical role. This issue arises in various contexts, including financial and demographic data analysis, where rates and counts are closely intertwined. Existing methods for reversing the process of aggregating and rounding data, often called the "disaggregation problem," are reviewed in this study. A new approach is proposed to address these problems, a specific example is provided, and the proposed method is tested for accuracy through data generated and real-world datasets.

Researchers investigated the two-dimensional centered honeycomb antiferromagnetic structure of GdInO$_3$,
confirming its hexagonal crystal lattice and Verwey transition at 122 K. Further analysis revealed a
magnetic phase transition into a hexagonal-centered honeycomb antiferromagnetic state at 23 K. Neutron diffraction studies showed GdInO$_3$'s magnetic structure to be hexagonal, aligned with its crystallographic axes and containing two magnetic sublattices with opposite spin directions.
